page: Amazon Web Services x2iedn.16xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. Powered by a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor, the instance provides 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores, backed by 54 MB of L3 cache and support for AVX-512 vector extensions. It delivers an extreme memory-to-vCPU ratio, provisioning 2048 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz alongside 1900 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD instance storage and a 50 Gbps baseline network interface.

Benchmark results highlight strong throughput across parallel compute tasks, with top-quartile performance in stress-ng multi-core testing (61,947.26), PassMark CPU score (56,826.42), and PassMark database operations (26,144.88). The platform also demonstrates strong results in multi-threaded compilation and CPU-based LLM token generation for smaller model sizes. Conversely, single-thread performance benchmarks such as Geekbench single-core (1688.0) and stress-ng single-core (1893.9) reflect mid-tier metrics consistent with standard Intel Ice Lake enterprise deployments.

Hardware resource allocation delivers significant density for large in-memory estates, consolidating high compute and 2 TB of RAM into a single node. The inclusion of high-speed local NVMe storage provides low-latency swap, caching, or temporary scratch space, offsetting potential disk bottlenecks. While the specialized resource profile commands an investment aligned with enterprise hardware, the extreme memory footprint minimizes the need to distribute workloads across multi-node clusters, lowering networking synchronization overhead.

The x2iedn.16xlarge is best suited for memory-bound applications, including large-scale in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, massive Redis or Memcached caching tiers, real-time analytics engines, relational database warehousing, and electronic design automation (EDA).
